name: XML Injection (aka Blind XPath Injection)
principle: The product inserts untrusted data into XML markup without neutralizing XML special elements such as <, >, ", ', and &. Attacker-controlled data can become XML syntax, nodes, attributes, or XML/XPath commands before downstream processing.
detection_signals: Java string concatenation or String.format builds XML/SOAP with request.getParameter(...) inside tags or attributes
C sprintf/snprintf/strcat builds '<tag>%s</tag>' or 'attr="%s"' with untrusted input
C++ std::string operator+ or std::ostringstream builds XML tags/attributes with tainted variables
XPathFactory.newXPath().compile(...) or evaluate(...) receives an expression concatenated with user input
XQuery/XPath/SOAP XML payload assembled by template replacement such as xml.replace("${name}", input)
User input is inserted into XML attribute value without escapeXml/forXml/writeAttribute
User input is inserted into XML text node without escapeXml/forXml/writeCharacters/setTextContent
negative_signals: Java DOM createElement(...) plus setTextContent(...) is used for user text
StAX XMLStreamWriter.writeCharacters(...) or writeAttribute(...) is used for user data
dom4j Element.setText(...) or addAttribute(...) is used instead of XML string concatenation
JAXB/XML marshalling is used from typed objects without raw XML string templates
Apache Commons Text StringEscapeUtils.escapeXml10(...) or OWASP Encoder Encode.forXml(...) is applied before concatenation
Server-side allowlist regex rejects XML metacharacters before XML construction
false_defense_traps: Denylist filters only '<' but not '&', '>', quotes, or entity forms
Client-side JavaScript validation is the only XML metacharacter check
Wrapping input in CDATA without blocking ']]>' allows CDATA breakout
Escaping text-node data reused later inside XML attributes or XPath expressions
Fixing XXE parser flags does not neutralize XML markup injection in constructed XML
verification_focus: Can attacker-controlled data reach XML/XPath/XQuery/SOAP syntax construction without XML-context-safe encoding or builder APIs?

consequence_chains.trigger: Input closes an existing tag and injects a new privileged node or attribute
consequence_chains.consequence: Modify application data, bypass authorization, or impersonate another user

consequence_chains.trigger: Input is concatenated into an XPath expression evaluated over XML data
consequence_chains.consequence: Read or modify unauthorized XML data via XPath injection

consequence_chains.trigger: Input is concatenated into an XQuery expression
consequence_chains.consequence: Execute unintended XML data queries or updates

consequence_chains.trigger: Injected markup creates malformed XML consumed by a parser
consequence_chains.consequence: Availability impact through parser errors or failed processing

patch_principle: Build XML with DOM, StAX, JAXB, or equivalent APIs instead of string concatenation.
Encode untrusted data for the exact XML context: text node, attribute, XPath, or XQuery.
Use strict server-side allowlists for fields with constrained business formats.
Parameterize or safely bind variables for XPath/XQuery when the API supports it.
Reject malformed XML metacharacter input when free-form XML markup is not allowed.
